text:
Andrew Connors receives 2026 Governor's Award for Excellence in the Arts
ABQ Times
Albuquerque Museum Director Andrew Connors has been named a recipient of the 2026 Governor's Award for Excellence in the Arts, according to a July 31 announcement from the City of Albuquerque’s Department of Arts & Culture. The award is one of New Mexico's highest honors, recognizing extraordinary contributions to the arts.
The Governor's Awards are presented annually by New Mexico Arts and the New Mexico Arts Commission. Connors is among eight recipients for 2026. “It is such an honor to be listed among this accomplished group of creatives and educators,” said Connors. “It has always been a joy to elevate the work of our state’s dynamic artists and introduce our community to the ideas of such powerful thinkers. Public museums provide these educational opportunities every day.”
Since taking on his role as director, Connors has expanded access to exhibitions, collections, and educational programming at Albuquerque Museum while deepening connections with Albuquerque’s artistic heritage. Before becoming director, he served as curator of art at the museum, focusing on exhibitions that highlight Hispanic, Latino, Native American, and folk art.
Mayor Tim Keller said, "Art of all kinds holds a special prominence here, and Andrew has helped elevate that at the Albuquerque Museum. This award is well-earned recognition for his vision and commitment to sharing New Mexico's stories." Connors' career includes leadership roles at Albuquerque Academy, National Hispanic Cultural Center, and Smithsonian American Art Museum; he was appointed in 2022 by President Joe Biden to serve on the U.S. Department of State's Cultural Properties Advisory Committee.
Other recipients this year include Adrián Aguirre (visual artist), Delbert Anderson (musician), Bill Barrett (sculptor), Anne Hillerman (author), Institute of American Indian Arts (organization), Eli Levin (painter), and Sam Scott (painter). The awards ceremony will take place October 15 at St. Francis Auditorium in Santa Fe’s New Mexico Museum of Art with an accompanying exhibition opening that day in the Governor’s Gallery at the State Capitol.
The City of Albuquerque maintains historic sites like KiMo Theatre—a venue known for its Pueblo Deco architecture—serving as cultural landmarks fostering community gatherings over decades; it operates under a council structure across nine geographic districts shaped by historical developments like railroads, according to city history resources.
